subject: placing a ggvis plot within shiny

messages.author: 1161df5ae7a276da
messages.subject: placing a ggvis plot within shiny
parts:
Hi all,

I'll try my best to get the language right; please forgive my butchering of the vocabulary.

Using what is already functional in ggvis, I am able to do some really neat things combining with shiny - stuff that I can show off within my company and say "look at what these RStudio folks can let me do!"

Where I am banging my head right now is how to size ggvis plots so that they will conform to the shiny layout.

To my best understanding, in ggvis opts, one specifies the width and height using pixels.

In the shiny/bootstrap framework, we have panels and columns, the width of which depend on the browser's width, and may be resized.

Is there a way (or could there be a way) to specify to ggvis or to shiny to take this plot, make the width according to the width of the container, and to specify an aspect ratio to be respected in case of window resizing?

Thanks,

Ian

messages.author: 912329a6ad1a6995
messages.subject: Re: placing a ggvis plot within shiny
parts:
Hi Jason,

Nothing yet (that I'm aware of). Having raised the issue, I'm trusting the RStudio folks to prioritize it appropriately.

I can only imagine that they have at least a dozen "top-priorities", and they will get to this in due time. 

My work-around has been to assume a dimension of 940*500, and then to use some css to enforce the width (I think RStudio does this for us). If I assume these dimensions, then I can assume each bootstrap column is 60 pixels wide and each gutter is 20 pixels wide (940 = 12*60 + 11*20). Given the number of columns I allot for a ggvis, I will set the width and height accordingly, using set_options().

Hope this helps,

Ian
